messages:
laura (support): FYI ACME (Dedicated, us-west-2) opened a high-sev ticket: mass 403s + tail latency spikes after autoscale event. Customer seeing repeated retries and billing surge. Ticket #ACME-1845
sam (sre): looking into it now
mike (infra): notified - autoscaler logs show repeated timeouts to cloud API during scale-up attempts
laura (support): customer paste: ```curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' https://api.redwood/v1/generate
# returns: 403```
laura (support): and a sample API error body: ```{"error":"auth_failed","code":403,"msg":"token invalid during node-rejoin"}```
natalie (dedicated-eng): I'm seeing OOM evictions on gpu-node-12 and gpu-node-13 around the same time - memory pressure -> preemption. Could be a noisy tenant running large continuous batches
ops-bot: :warning: alert: region-us-west-2.gpu_utilization=92% (sustained), free_nodes=1
mike (infra): kube events excerpt: ```14:01:03 Pod gpu-job-77 Evicted Reason=ExceededGPUMemory
14:03:10 HorizontalPodAutoscaler ScaleUp failed: error contacting cloudprovider: timeout
14:03:55 AuthService retry 5 -> 403 token-reissue failed```
devon (oncall): that sequence (eviction -> failed scale -> token churn) will cause bursts of 429/403s as clients retry. Are we reassigning tokens when nodes rejoin?
sam (sre): good q. Auth service logs show a token-mapping race when node id changes during reprovision. I'll dump auth logs for the window
laura (support): customer also reports a sudden billing delta: tokens consumed jumped ~2x for 30m while they retried. Billing flagged it as anomaly
billing-bot: alert: invoice-anomaly detected for customer ACME-1845, token_units +98% over 30m window
natalie (dedicated-eng): repro steps I ran locally: 1) start a long-running TP job with continuous batching (batch_size=64) on a 2-GPU reserved pool; 2) trigger a simulated node eviction -> memory usage spikes to 98% -> few seconds later autoscaler tries to add nodes but hits cloud API throttles -> node IDs rotate -> auth mapping invalidates tokens -> client retries -> exponential backoff saturates rate limiter.
laura (support): can we route ACME to another capacity pool while we fix? They agreed to a temporary reroute
mike (infra): temp route applied to backup pool in us-west-1 but needs token mapping patch so their existing tokens are valid there. Patching allocator to preserve node identity mapping during hot-swap (WIP). ETA ~12m
sam (sre): workaround posted to customer: reduce client retry aggressiveness and use fixed token refresh schedule; that'll cut duplicate consumption.
laura (support): after routing to us-west-1 latency improved for ACME but a handful of 403s still trickling in (some tokens invalidated mid-session)
devon (oncall): root cause hypothesis: (1) noisy tenant causes GPU memory pressure -> pod evictions, (2) autoscaler failed to scale because cloud provider requests throttled -> delayed reprovision, (3) node identity rotation + auth mapping race invalidated tokens -> clients retried and was charged. Next steps: collect allocator logs + auth-service logs + kube events for 13:58-14:10 window.
mike (infra): uploading alloc logs now: https://internal.redwood/alloc-logs/2110007777 (internal only)
sam (sre): grabbing auth-service logs and HPA metrics, will correlate with billing spike timestamp
laura (support): action items agreed: (A) infra: preserve node identity on reassign / patch allocator (mike) (B) sRE: confirm auth token mapping fix and add guard to avoid invalidation during reprovision (sam) (C) support/finance: review billing credit for ACME and notify (laura + billing-bot) (D) eng: investigate noisy tenant mitigation (natalie)
laura (support): I've told ACME we're routing them temporarily and investigating, next update in 30m :thumbsup:
sam (sre): will post follow-up with logs + final mitigation plan. If this extends >2h we'll open a formal postmortem.
laura (support): thanks team, keeping this thread as single point of truth.
